note: Legal shows Terms & Conditions on registration and requires acceptance. T&C TEXT is content, stored in the legal_conditions entity/table (versioned per language) and entered at /admin/config/people/legal; acceptances are in legal_accepted. Behaviour is config legal.settings (registration_terms_style 0=Scroll box/1=Scroll CSS/2=HTML/3=Page link, accept_every_login, except_roles, user_profile_display, ...). Baseline site has 0 conditions and shipped legal.settings defaults. Medium cases read back accept_every_login and registration_terms_style. Hard cases: create an English T&C version (verified via legal_conditions), and configure legal.settings to require acceptance every login + exempt the administrator role. Programmatic T&C creation uses Conditions::create() with version from legal_version().

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the Legal module enabled, where does an administrator enter the Terms & Conditions text that new users must accept, and what happens to existing users when the text changes?
evals.expected_output: Enter the terms at Configuration > People > Legal (/admin/config/people/legal, route legal.config_legal). Each save stores a new version in legal_conditions, and publishing a new version forces existing users to re-accept on their next login.

evals.prompt: How can I add a Terms & Conditions version programmatically (e.g. in an update hook) with the Legal module, and where is that text stored?
evals.expected_output: T&C text is a content entity, not config. Use Drupal\legal\Entity\Conditions::create([...])->save() with version/revision from legal_version('version', $lang), plus language, conditions (text), format, date, extras (serialized), changes. It is stored in the legal_conditions table.

evals.prompt: What display-style options does the Legal module offer for showing the Terms & Conditions on the registration form, and which config setting selects it?
evals.expected_output: The config legal.settings.registration_terms_style selects it: 0 = Scroll box (plain text), 1 = Scroll box (CSS), 2 = HTML text, 3 = Page link (accept label links to the terms, optionally in a modal). A matching login_terms_style controls the login/profile display.

evals.prompt: On this site, is the Legal module configured to make users accept the Terms & Conditions on every login, or only when the terms change? Inspect the live configuration and answer.
evals.expected_output: Users must accept on every login — legal.settings.accept_every_login is TRUE.

evals.prompt: Inspect the Legal module configuration on this site and tell me which display style is set for the Terms & Conditions on the registration form (name the style, not just a number).
evals.expected_output: It is set to HTML text — legal.settings.registration_terms_style is 2, which renders the terms as inline HTML.

evals.prompt: With the Legal module, I want everyone to have to re-agree to the Terms & Conditions each time they log in, except administrators who should never be bothered by it. Configure that and apply it to the site.
evals.expected_output: In legal.settings set accept_every_login to TRUE and add 'administrator' to except_roles (the list of role IDs exempt from the T&C requirement).
